newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch - Feb 20.
newsitem.headline: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch - Feb 20.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors likely to affect Philippine stocks on Thursday:
* On Wednesday, the Dow Jones fell 47.33 points to 7,020.13. PLDT's ADR rose $0 1/8 to $60 3/8.
* The peso closed unchanged at 26.340 to a U.S. dollar.
* The Philippine Stock Exchange composite index rose 9.09 points to 3,315.52.
* The Philippine interbank call loan average was unchanged at 10.5625 percent.
* China's paramount leader Deng Xiaoping died late Wednesday of complications from Parkinsons disease and a lung infection.

* The Philippine Times Journal says the Court of Appeals lifts the temporary restraining order issued on the privatisation of the Metropolitan Waterworks and Sewerage System (MWSS) removing the stumbling block to the privatisation of the country's biggest water utility. (PHILIPPINE STAR)
* BusinessWorld says the International Monetary Fund is inclined to hold the government to its original commitment to have all the components of the Comprehensive Tax Reform Package passed by June.

* Manila Times says Finance Minister Roberto de Ocampo is not amenable to the proposal to extend by another five years the privilege of companies registered with the Board of Investments to import capital goods while paying no or minimal duties.
* Malaya says the National Power Corp 1996 net income rose by 41.6 percent to 5.542 billion from 3.914 billion pesos in 1995.

* Philippine Times Journal says the Philippine Savings Bank, a subsidiary of Metropolitan Bank and Trust Co, is beefing up its authorised capital stock to 4.25 billion pesos from three billionm pesos.
* Times Journal also says C&P Homes reported a preliminary unaudited net income for 1996 of 2.730 billion pesos, 30 percent from 2.011 billion pesos. (MANILA CHRONICLE)
